newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Dollar skids lower after Bonn pledge on EMU.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Dollar skids lower after Bonn pledge on EMU.

text.p: The dollar lost its edge against the mark on Wednesday after German Chancellor Helmut Kohl declared that Bonn remained on track for monetary union despite a bruising row with the powerful Bundesbank.
The dollar hit four-week highs in early trade as the German government retreated from controversial plans to revalue assets to help meet make the grade for EMU.
But a series of statements by Kohl, Finance Minister Theo Waigel and Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer reversed the wobbly foreign exchange market and the mark recovered.

The Bundesbank row appeared to have little impact on German shares, which put on moderate gains along with the Paris bourse. But government bond markets were unsettled over concerns about events in Germany and interest rate worries in Britain.

Chancellor Kohl threw his weight fully behind Waigel in parliament after his embattled ally lost his grab for Bundesbank gold to help Germany qualify for the euro by filling a gap in government finances.
Kohl told a stormy session of parliament that Waigel would stay in office and Germany would still meet the strict Maastricht criteria for the launch of monetary union (EMU) in 1999.

Under a Bonn-Bundesbank compromise, funds from the asset revaluation will now be transferred to the government in 1998 instead of this year, which the market saw as increasing the chances that a broad group of countries would launch a soft euro.

"The mark is in all sorts of problems in Europe because of the gold row and although the heat has come off that problem, the general story the market is fixed on is on a soft euro," said David Brown, chief European economist at Bear Stearns in London.
The dollar was nearly a pfennig higher at one point, but by 1430 GMT it was quoted at 1.7274 marks and 116.13 yen, compared with 1.7263 marks and 116.06 yen in late European trading on Tuesday.
Europe's major stock markets all showed gains in the morning, but London slipped into the minus column as Wall Street made a weak start, with the Dow standing 21 points down after the first hour.
Paris clawed its way back from opening losses as the market waited for new Prime Minister Lionel Jospin to name his cabinet.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index was off its highs but still showing a rise of 14.12 points, or 0.54 percent, at 2,638.61 by 1430 GMT as the market continued to recover following the Socialist election victory on Sunday.
Dealers said the market was supported by dollar firmness, rises on other stockmarkets and expectations of a moderate Socialist government.
Hotel group Accor gave back its early rise, falling just over one percent to 840 francs after it forecast 25 percent higher profit from the budget sector this year.
Leading British shares staged a bounce in the morning on the back of Wall Street's firm overnight close.
But by mid-afternoon, the benchmark FTSE 100 was down 1.3 points at 4,556.5.
British shares hesitated earlier after the Purchasing Mangers Index rose for the 11th consecutive month in May, which dealers said reinforced the view that British interest rates are poised to rise.

Fears that a strong set of U.S. unemployment figures, due on Friday, could also trigger a Federal Reserve interest rate hike kept many players on the sidelines and are likely to cap the FTSE's near-term gains, dealers said.
In Frankfurt, Germany's 30-share DAX index played catch up in bourse trade to match gains in electronic screen trade late on Tuesday.
It closed up about one percent, but traders said the market lacked impetus to forge more significant gains. In later screen-based trade, the IBIS DAX index was up 2.06 points at 1430 GMT.
The soothing words from both sides on the Bundesbank-Bonn gold revaluation row were seen as mostly market neutral.
CURRENCIES AT1430 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.7273 marks and 116.13 yen compared with 1.7263 marks and 116.06 yen in late European trading on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1430 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 1.2 points, or 0.03 percent, at 4,556.5.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 14.12 points, or 0.54 percent, at 2,638.61.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed up 36.1 points, or 1.0 percent, at 3,661.84.
PRECIOUS METALS

Gold fixed at $341.75 compared with $342.40 in the morning. Silver was up a cent at $4.75. Platinum was $2.50 easier after frantic morning trading at $414.50, while palladium was off its high but $14.90 up at $209.90.
